messages:
raj: Heads-up — onboarding request for a new AWS account just hit prod needs. Account 987654321098 currently has GPU instance quotas at 0 in us-west-2. We need 12 p4d and 16 g5. Also ENI limit looks low (currently 50), we should request bump to 1000. Can someone open a support case and escalate?

alex: I can open the case. Need the business justification and expected start date. Also, do we have a TAM for this account or is it standard support?

raj: Start date asap — trying to get a cluster provisioned for infra stress tests next week (target Mon). Biz justification: "Production inference fleet for customer pilot, requires reserved p4d/g5 capacity for low-latency evals; short notice due to contract milestone."

alex: Cool. Opening now. Posting case IDs here when created.

alex: (case created) aws-support: case 12345678901 opened — EC2 quota increase request for p4d/g5 & ENI in us-west-2. Link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=12345678901  Ticket owner: premium-support.

maria: Can you CC finance/procurement on the case? We may need to accept a capacity-based commitment or on-demand pricing. @alex please add procurement@redwood.com to the thread.

alex: Added procurement email to case. Also attached the cost projection: ``Estimated monthly GPU runway: p4d x12 + g5 x16 ~ $120k/month (spot not viable for this workload).``

cloud-bot: [automated] Support case 12345678901 status changed: "Awaiting AWS review" — last update 2025-04-12 15:10 UTC

sre-oncall: FYI we should also request a soft quota on Elastic IP and SG rules in the same region — high-node counts can hit those limits. I'll paste the commands to check current quotas:```
# check EC2 quotas
aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-1216C47A --region us-west-2  # ENI
aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-34B43A08 --region us-west-2  # p4d instances per region
```

aws-support: Update on case 12345678901 — assigned to EC2 quota team. We see a standard process for boosts; to expedite, please provide an architecture diagram and expected IP ranges, and confirm whether instances are for production (yes/no). If production, we can route to Priority queue.

raj: Replying in the case: attached diagram, confirming production pilot, start date 2025-04-21, contact point me (raj@redwood.com) and @maria. Requesting Priority escalation.

cloud-bot: [automated] AWS responded to case 12345678901 — status: "Information required" (2025-04-12 16:02 UTC)

alex: I put up the architecture doc and a short note saying we need a rapid turnaround due to contract. Also asked for estimated ETA for approval.

aws-support: Quick update — we pushed this to Priority queue per your note. Preliminary approval likely but needs capacity confirmation with EC2 provisioning. Estimated response ETA: 24-48h. Case 12345678901 -> escalation code ESCL-7592.

maria: Great. If AWS needs capacity reservations, we need procurement to approve spend. @procurement can you pre-authorize up to $150k/month for the pilot if we get the quota?

alex: Noted. I'll keep watching the case and post updates. If no approval in 48h we should escalate to our TAM and sales rep.

sre-oncall: One more thing — when quotas increase, remember to set up placement group configs and EFA drivers for the p4d fleet. I'll prep a launch playbook and post it here.

cloud-bot: [automated] Case 12345678901 updated: Escalation ESCL-7592 acknowledged by EC2 field team (2025-04-13 09:20 UTC)

aws-support: Final note for this thread: if you need immediate capacity today, we can offer a temporary workaround by provisioning in us-east-1 where quotas are available; let us know if region move is acceptable.

raj: Prefer us-west-2 due to data residency and latency requirements. Marking east fallback as last-resort. Thanks for the push so far.

alex: Closing out here for now — will reopen thread with AWS updates. :thumbsup:
